alexander.title: Alexander
alexander.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
alexander.note: A coppersmith who did Paul great harm, and Paul warns Timothy about him.

antioch-2.title: Antioch
antioch-2.note: The other Antioch, in Pisidia. Paul preached there with some success until local Jewish leaders drove him out, and later he came back to strengthen the church.

aquila.title: Aquila
aquila.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
aquila.note: A Jewish tentmaker from Pontus. He and his wife Priscilla had been expelled from Rome with other Jews, met Paul in Corinth, and worked beside him. Churches met in their home in more than one city.

asia.title: Asia
asia.note: Not the continent. The Roman province of Asia, in western Asia Minor, with Ephesus among its churches, and the region the seven churches of Revelation belonged to.

carpus.title: Carpus
carpus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
carpus.note: Paul had left a cloak and some books or parchments with him at Troas, and asks Timothy to pick them up on the way.

christ.title: Christ
christ.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
christ.note: A title, not a surname. It is the Greek for the Hebrew Messiah, the anointed one, and the New Testament gives it to Jesus of Nazareth as the king, priest and deliverer the Old Testament promised. His life and ministry are under Jesus.

claudia.title: Claudia
claudia.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
claudia.note: Paul passes her greetings to Timothy from Rome, with those of Pudens, Linus and Eubulus. People have tried to match her with a Claudia in Martial's poems who married a Pudens, but the shared names are all that idea rests on.

corinth.title: Corinth
corinth.note: Paul stayed eighteen months in this rich trading city on the isthmus, and the church he planted got two of his longest letters. He stood before the proconsul Gallio there, whose dated term helps fix Paul's timeline. An inscription found at Corinth names an Erastus who paid for a pavement, likely the city treasurer of Romans 16:23.

crescens.title: Crescens
crescens.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
crescens.note: By the time Paul wrote his last letter from prison, Crescens had gone to Galatia; tradition, not Scripture, has him founding churches in Gaul.

dalmatia.title: Dalmatia
dalmatia.note: Titus had gone to Dalmatia by the time Paul wrote from his last imprisonment in Rome. It was the rough coast along the eastern Adriatic, part of the province of Illyricum, roughly modern Croatia and Montenegro. Rome had put down a big revolt there under Tiberius in AD 9.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling the largest territory Israel ever held, which Solomon then inherited. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

demas.title: Demas
demas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
demas.note: With Paul in his imprisonment, and then gone. Paul writes that Demas deserted him because he loved this present world.

ephesus.title: Ephesus
ephesus.note: The chief city of Roman Asia, with the temple of Artemis and a theatre for some twenty five thousand. Paul stayed about three years and the silversmiths rioted over lost trade. Later it was one of the seven churches of Revelation, and tradition says John died and was buried there.

erastus.title: Erastus
erastus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
erastus.note: Paul's companion, and in Romans the city treasurer of Corinth. An inscription found at Corinth names an Erastus who paid for a pavement in return for an aedileship.

eubulus.title: Eubulus
eubulus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
eubulus.note: One of the Christians in Rome whose greetings Paul sends Timothy, with Pudens, Linus and Claudia.

eunice.title: Eunice
eunice.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
eunice.note: Timothy's mother, a Jewish believer married to a Greek. Paul says her faith was real, and that she and Lois, Timothy's grandmother, raised him on the Scriptures from a child.

galatia.title: Galatia
galatia.note: Gaulish tribes from Europe settled this part of central Asia Minor in the third century BC, and Rome made it a province in 25 BC. Paul wrote one of his sharpest letters to its churches, against teachers who wanted Gentile believers circumcised.

hermogenes.title: Hermogenes
hermogenes.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
hermogenes.note: He deserted Paul. Paul names him with Phygellus in Asia Minor and sets them against Onesiphorus, who did not.

hymenaeus.title: Hymenaeus
hymenaeus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
hymenaeus.note: Paul names him twice, both times as a warning. In one letter he and Alexander are handed over to Satan for blasphemy; in the other he and Philetus are teaching that the resurrection has already happened, and some have lost their faith over it. He was probably at Ephesus.

iconium.title: Iconium
iconium.note: Modern Konya, in central Asia Minor. Paul and Barnabas came here after being thrown out of Antioch in Pisidia, and a crowd of Jews and Gentiles turned on them, so they fled to Lystra and Derbe. Paul came back later to strengthen the church.

jambres.title: Jambres
jambres.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jambres.note: Paul names Jannes and Jambres as the men who opposed Moses, and so a warning about anyone who resists the truth. Exodus has Pharaoh's magicians copy some of the signs but never names them; the names come from Jewish tradition.

jannes.title: Jannes
jannes.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jannes.note: The other of the two Egyptian magicians who stood against Moses before Pharaoh. Exodus does not name either, and Paul takes the names from a well-known tradition.

jesus.title: Jesus
jesus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jesus.note: Born in Bethlehem to Mary and raised in Nazareth in Galilee. Around thirty he began teaching in parables, healing, and gathering twelve disciples, until he was arrested in Jerusalem at Passover, tried before the council and Pontius Pilate, and crucified. His followers said he rose bodily three days later, and the New Testament names him the Messiah, God's own Son become human.

linus.title: Linus
linus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
linus.note: Paul passes on his greeting to Timothy from Rome. Irenaeus records a tradition that he was the first bishop of Rome after Peter and Paul, though the New Testament says nothing about any office he held.

lois.title: Lois
lois.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
lois.note: Timothy's grandmother. Paul says the faith he sees in Timothy lived first in her and then in her daughter Eunice.

lucas.title: Lucas
lucas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
lucas.note: The Latin form of Luke, Paul's travelling companion and doctor. Early tradition gives him the Gospel of Luke and Acts, which would make him the one Gentile writer in the New Testament.

lystra.title: Lystra
lystra.note: A Roman colony in the wild hills of Lycaonia, and Timothy's hometown. Paul healed a man lame from birth there and the crowd tried to sacrifice to him and Barnabas as Hermes and Zeus. Then Paul's opponents turned the same crowd, and they stoned him and left him for dead.

marcus.title: Marcus
marcus.about: Levite living at the time of the New Testament
marcus.note: John Mark. He set out with Paul and Barnabas and left partway through the first journey, and that later split the two men in a sharp quarrel. Peter calls him his son, and early church tradition says he wrote the Gospel of Mark from Peter's preaching.

miletus.title: Miletus
miletus.note: About thirty-five miles south of Ephesus, a port in Ionia. Paul, hurrying to be in Jerusalem for Pentecost, called the elders of Ephesus down to Miletus and gave them his farewell, warning of false teachers to come. He later left Trophimus there sick. Silt from the Meander River has since pushed the coast away, and the old theatre now stands miles inland.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

onespiphorus.title: Onespiphorus
onespiphorus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
onespiphorus.note: The spelling is a slip in the source data for Onesiphorus. He was a believer from Ephesus who went looking for Paul in his Roman imprisonment and looked after him without being ashamed of the chains.

paul.title: Paul
paul.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
paul.note: Born Saul, a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin and a Roman citizen from Tarsus. He trained as a Pharisee under Gamaliel and hunted the early church. Then the risen Christ met him in a blinding vision.

philetus.title: Philetus
philetus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
philetus.note: Paul warns Timothy about him and Hymenaeus, who were saying the resurrection had already happened. Paul says that kind of talk spreads "like gangrene."

phygellus.title: Phygellus
phygellus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
phygellus.note: In his last imprisonment in Rome, Paul writes that everyone in Asia turned away from him, and he names Phygellus and Hermogenes.

prisca.title: Prisca
prisca.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
prisca.note: Paul's formal Latin form of Priscilla, used in his letters.

pudens.title: Pudens
pudens.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
pudens.note: He sends greetings to Timothy with Claudia, Linus and Eubulus at the close of 2 Timothy. A Christian at Rome, and attempts to tie him to a Roman senator lack real proof.

rome.title: Rome
rome.note: Capital of the empire that ruled Judea through the whole New Testament period. Paul wrote to the church there, and Acts ends with him in the city as a prisoner, his case appealed to Caesar.

thessalonica.title: Thessalonica
thessalonica.note: The capital of Macedonia, a busy port on the Via Egnatia. Paul preached in the synagogue there for a few weeks before opposition drove him on to Berea. Luke calls the city officials politarchs, an unusual title.

timotheus.title: Timotheus
timotheus.note: Timothy, from Lystra, with a Jewish mother and a Greek father. Paul took him along on his travels and trusted him with hard errands to churches in trouble, and two of Paul's letters are addressed to him.

titus.title: Titus
titus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
titus.note: A Gentile convert who worked with Paul. He carried a hard letter to the church at Corinth and brought back word of how it landed. Paul later left him in Crete to organize the churches, and the letter to Titus is the instructions.

troas.title: Troas
troas.note: It was a port on the northwest coast of Asia Minor near old Troy. Paul had his vision of the Macedonian man there, come over and help us, and on a later visit he raised Eutychus from the dead during a sermon that went all night.

trophimus.title: Trophimus
trophimus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
trophimus.note: A Gentile from Ephesus who traveled with Paul. People in Jerusalem thought Paul had taken him into the temple, and that started the riot that ended with Paul under arrest.

tychicus.title: Tychicus
tychicus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
tychicus.note: He carried Paul's letters, Ephesians and Colossians among them, and told the churches in person how Paul was doing.
